episode_title: Swap Broker Fees, Run on a Napkin: What Volume Pays the Bills?
summary: Jules and Mira model how much a Chainflip swap broker can earn from affiliate fees, walking through fee tiers, breakeven volume, payback time and three integration scenarios, from a niche wallet to a regional exchange to an aggregator.
hook: Adding swaps to your wallet or exchange and charging a small fee sounds like easy money. But how much volume do you actually need before it pays for itself? Jules brings his teenage car wash side hustle, Mira brings the spreadsheet, and together they run the real numbers.
key_points: Chainflip charges a flat 0.10% protocol fee; brokers can add their own fee from 0 to 1000 bps, paid straight to their address in the destination asset
At $2,000/month in costs, breakeven volume is $4M at 5 bps, $2M at 10 bps and $800K at 25 bps
A niche wallet doing $50K/month at 15 bps earns $75, while an exchange with $30M of existing volume earns $15K to $30K
Over the last 30 days the network did $517.49M in volume, so 10 bps across all of it would be about $517K in potential broker revenue
The simple formula: users who'd swap x average swap size x your fee, minus costs
keywords: how much can a swap broker earn

chapters.title: Cold open: the tire shine dollar
The size of the pie and how to run your own math

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: [grinning] Mira, I was a broker once.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: [deadpan] You sold knives door to door. That's not a broker.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: No, before that. The car wash. Gus charged eight bucks a wash, and I talked him into letting me offer tire shine on top. One extra dollar. Gus kept his eight, I kept my dollar.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: And how'd that go?

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Saturday? Rich. Tuesday morning? Three cars, and one of them was Gus.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: [amused] Okay, that is weirdly today's episode.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Welcome to Cross-Chain Daily. I'm Mira, he's Jules, and today we're running the numbers on how much a swap broker can actually earn from affiliate fees on Chainflip.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: So start me at zero. What's a broker here?

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Anyone who sends swaps through the protocol with their own broker address. A wallet, an exchange, an aggregator. Chainflip takes a flat ten basis point protocol fee on every swap. That's zero point one percent.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: And a basis point is...

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: A hundredth of a percent. A hundred basis points is one percent.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Got it. And then the broker adds their tire shine.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: [half-laughing] Yes. The broker sets their own fee on top, anywhere from zero to a thousand basis points, so zero to ten percent. And per the article, it goes straight to your address. No revenue share back to Chainflip.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Wait. Gus took half my tire shine money by July.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: No Gus here. Your fee comes out of the swap output, and you get paid in the destination asset. No invoices, no waiting, no minimum payout.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Okay, so how much money are we talking?

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: The article models three tiers. Low-cost is five basis points. On a hundred thousand dollars of monthly volume, that's fifty dollars. On a million, five hundred.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Fifty bucks. That's, um, fifty tire shines.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Middle tier is ten basis points, same as the protocol fee. A hundred thousand gets you a hundred dollars. A million gets you a thousand.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: And premium?

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Twenty-five basis points. Two hundred fifty on a hundred thousand, two thousand five hundred on a million. The article says premium works when you're adding real value, like better UX, support or specialized routing.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Right. I tried a five dollar tire shine once. Called it Deluxe. Same spray bottle.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: How many did you sell?

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: [sheepish] Zero. A guy in a minivan laughed at me.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: [dry] Price without value. Noted.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Okay, real question. When does this pay for itself?

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Breakeven. Say your integration costs about two thousand dollars a month to run. Servers, monitoring, some maintenance. At five basis points you need four million in monthly volume. At ten, two million. At twenty-five, eight hundred thousand.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: And building it in the first place?

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Their example is forty hours of developer time at a hundred fifty an hour. Six thousand dollars upfront. Netting a thousand a month, which is ten basis points on a million with no running costs, you're paid back in six months.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Six months. Okay, that's not bad.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Now the scenarios. First, a niche wallet. Five thousand active users, two percent of them swap each month, average swap five hundred dollars.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: So, fifty swaps? No. A hundred?

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: A hundred swaps, fifty thousand dollars a month. At fifteen basis points, that's seventy-five dollars.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: [quick, cutting in] Seventy-five?

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Seventy-five. The article says that only makes sense if the integration is trivial, or strategic for other reasons.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: That's my Tuesday morning. Three cars and Gus.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Second, a regional exchange that already has volume. Five hundred users a day swapping cross-chain, average two thousand dollars. Over thirty days, that's thirty million.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Thirty million? From five hundred people a day?

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Volume you already have is the whole trick. At ten basis points, thirty thousand a month. Even at five, to stay competitive, fifteen thousand.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: That's my Saturday. Line around the block.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Third, an aggregator. You only get the volume when Chainflip has the best rate. Say five million a month at eight basis points. Four thousand dollars, stacked with fees from every other protocol you route through.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Okay, zoom out. How big is the whole car wash?

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: At the time of writing, five hundred seventeen point four nine million dollars in swap volume over thirty days, across forty-two thousand six hundred twenty-six swaps. So the average swap is about twelve thousand one hundred forty dollars.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Way bigger than my wallet guy's five hundred.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Way bigger. All-time DEX volume is eight point three two eight billion. And one point zero four million in protocol fees over the last thirty days. Broker fees are on top of that.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: So if every broker charged ten basis points on everything...

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: About five hundred seventeen thousand a month in potential broker revenue. The real number is lower, since not all volume comes through brokers. But that's the size of the pie.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Here's my pushback, though. These numbers assume every month looks the same.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: They do, and the article says so. Real integrations rarely see steady volume. Baselines, not promises.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Saturdays and Tuesdays.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: [amused] Saturdays and Tuesdays. Fine, the tire shine goes in the spreadsheet. Held up.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Full column? Not Half held up?

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Full column. Don't make it weird.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: So how does somebody run this for their own app?

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Three variables. Realistic volume, fee tier, costs. Guess what share of your users would swap cross-chain, multiply by the average swap size, apply your fee. That's monthly gross. Subtract costs.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: And if it's positive?

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: And it grows as you grow, it makes sense. Starting from zero users, broker fees alone won't carry it. But having the feature and keeping users around might still be worth it.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: [thoughtful] So the fee is the easy part. The volume is the whole business.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Yep. Volume you already have does more than a fancy fee tier.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: The full article is linked in the show notes, and live numbers are on Chainflip Scan. Not financial advice.

lines.speaker: jules
lines.text: Go sell some tire shine. Stay native.

lore.note: As a teen at Gus's car wash (eight bucks a wash) he sold a one-dollar tire shine add-on and kept the dollar; great on Saturdays, dead on Tuesday mornings (three cars, one was Gus). Gus started taking half by July. 'Saturdays and Tuesdays' is now his picture of uneven volume, and the tire shine dollar is his picture of a broker fee.
He once tried a five-dollar 'Deluxe' tire shine (same spray bottle), sold zero, and got laughed at by a guy in a minivan. His picture of charging a premium fee without adding value.
Put the tire shine in the full 'Held up' column of her Jules-analogy spreadsheet, not 'Half held up', and told him not to make it weird.
